description: Sample request bodies for POST /v/addItem endpoint
note: All sensitive data must be encrypted client-side using AES-256-GCM before sending. These examples show the structure with placeholder base64 values.

field_descriptions.title: Optional - Item title (string). Can be plain text for search/filtering.
field_descriptions.encrypted_data: Required - Base64 encoded AES-256-GCM ciphertext containing all sensitive item data. Must be valid base64.
field_descriptions.iv: Required - Base64 encoded 12-byte initialization vector. When decoded, must be exactly 12 bytes (16 base64 characters).
field_descriptions.field_count: Required - Number of encrypted fields in this item (number >= 0).
field_descriptions.attachment_count: Required - Number of attachments linked to this item (number >= 0).
field_descriptions.folderId: Optional - MongoDB ObjectId string of the folder this item belongs to, or null for items in Personal safe.
field_descriptions.tags: Optional - Array of tag strings for organization.
field_descriptions.isFavorite: Optional - Boolean indicating if item is favorited (default: false).

validation_notes.iv_validation: IV must be exactly 12 bytes when base64 decoded. A 12-byte IV will be exactly 16 base64 characters (no padding). Example: '41cwblOzDiuI8mcI' decodes to 12 bytes.
validation_notes.encrypted_data_validation: encrypted_data must be valid base64 encoded string. The actual encrypted content depends on your encryption implementation.
validation_notes.category_validation: Category must be a non-empty string. Common values: 'password', 'financial', 'notes', etc.
validation_notes.field_count_validation: field_count must be a number >= 0. Represents the number of encrypted fields stored in encrypted_data.
validation_notes.attachment_count_validation: attachment_count must be a number >= 0. If files are uploaded via multipart/form-data, this should match the number of files.

usage_example.curl:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5001/v/addItem \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN' \
  -d @sample_request.json
usage_example.note: Replace YOUR_JWT_TOKEN with a valid JWT token obtained from authentication endpoint.
